query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for structural use under extreme-temperature conditions, what single intervention could improve high-temperature oxygen resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the untreated alloy, defines the temperature, atmosphere, and exposure conditions under which it should work, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding 5 wt% Cr to a refractory high-entropy alloy will improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance by forming a protective Cr2O3 oxide layer, reducing the oxidation rate by 30% relative to the untreated alloy at 1000°C in air.
generation.material_initial_state: Refractory high-entropy alloy in its as-cast state
generation.intervention: Adding 5 wt% Cr to the alloy composition
generation.conditions: Exposure to air at 1000°C for 100 hours
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a Cr2O3 oxide layer
generation.mechanism: The added Cr reacts with oxygen to form a protective Cr2O3 layer, reducing the diffusion of oxygen into the alloy and thereby decreasing the oxidation rate
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 900-1100°C, Atmosphere: air, Exposure time: 100 hours
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement in oxygen resistance may vary depending on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the oxidation rates of the Cr-added alloy and the untreated alloy at 1000°C in air for 100 hours
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the oxidation rate of the Cr-added alloy is not at least 20% lower than that of the untreated alloy, the hypothesis is falsified
